```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(psych)
```

The aim of this SSA is to practice concepts of reliability, specifically the reliability coefficient and Cohen’s kappa.

We use three data sets, `biopt0`, `biopt1` and `biopt2`, all containing the same data in different formats being useful for the different analyses. 12 tumor tissue biopsies were scored by 33 students (column DeviceId is the student number) and a block-coordinator (deviceId = 34). The score range from 1 to 4 and measure tumor grade. Each tissue sample has been scored twice where sample 1 is the same as sample 13 (2 ~ 14, 3 ~ 15,…) in data set `biopt0`.

# Data

```{r}
data(biopt0)
data(biopt1)
data(biopt2)
```

# Exercise 5
We will now calculate the reliability coefficient using a mixed model.

```{r}
dataMM <- biopt2[biopt2$DeviceID == ChosenID, ]
mixedmod <- lmer(score ~ herhaling + (1 | uniekbiopt), data = dataMM)

summary(mixedmod)
ci2P(confint(mixedmod))
```

## a
Study the output for fixed effects. Inspect the P-value for “herhaling”. What is the interpretation of this P-value?

**fillin**:  

## b
Study the output for the `Random effects`. What does it mean and how do you interpret the standard deviations? Calculate the reliability coefficient.

**fillin**:
